small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — M is tiny (one BLOCK_M=128 covers all rows). Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N in {128,256}, BLOCK_K in {32,64}, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4, and drop GROUP_M swizzle (set GROUP_M=1) since there is only one row group anyway; this removes wasted swizzle math.
- Softmax over 16384 cols with BLOCK_SIZE=4096 forces 4 sequential chunks plus a 2nd pass re-reading from HBM. Increase BLOCK_SIZE to 16384 (single-pass, row fits) with num_warps=16 and num_stages=2, eliminating the second load pass entirely.
- In the GEMM K-loop, replace the per-iteration K-tail mask with a peeled tail (full-tile loads when k+BLOCK_K<=K, masked load only on the last iteration) so the hot loop has unmasked `tl.load`s — this lets Triton issue wider cp.async on Ada.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the GEMM epilogue using a split-K / row-persistent design: since M=128 fits in a single program-row dimension, launch one program per row that streams all N=16384 outputs, computing dot-products tile-by-tile across K and accumulating row-max and row-sum online — then a second persistent pass writes normalized exp. This removes the full intermediate write/read of the 128x16384 logits tensor (~8 MB) between GEMM and softmax.
- Alternatively, keep GEMM separate but make it a split-K kernel: with K=16384 and only 128 rows, a single-K kernel underutilizes the SMs. Split K across the grid (e.g., SPLIT_K=4-8) with atomic-add or a small reduction kernel to fully occupy the 128 SMs of the 4090.
- Store the weight as transposed (N-major contiguous) once at init so the inner load of W is a contiguous BLOCK_N row vector instead of strided BLOCK_K x BLOCK_N tiles; pair this with vectorized 128-bit loads.
